summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31% YoY to Rs 1,329 million, with EBITDA of Rs 777 million (58.45% margin) and Cordelia Sky delivered early.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs 1,329 million, up 31% YoY, with PAT of Rs 585 million. H1 FY27 revenue was stated as Rs 3,230 billion (likely Rs 3,230 million, a transcript inconsistency), up 16% YoY, with H1 PAT of Rs 813 million. Cordelia Sky arrived in Mumbai on schedule, about a month early, with sailing set to start 23 October 2026, adding roughly 126% to capacity. Fuel cost per APCD roughly rose 72% in Q2 YoY (Rs 2,471 vs Rs 1,434), which management said cost about Rs 28 crore in H1 that was partly offset by fuel surcharges and cost savings.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 3,230 billion as stated (appears to be Rs 3,230 million)

segments.name: Cruise operations (Empress, Sky, SUN)
segments.commentary: Empress is the operating vessel with 796 rooms and 2,005 beds. Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) arrived early and starts sailing 23 October 2026. SUN, a sister ship slightly larger, is due in about 11 months.

guidance_outlook: Sky revenue to begin contributing from H2 FY27, with larger benefits as utilisation ramps up.

Management hopes fuel costs ease in Q3 and Q4, and expects fuel cost impact to be neutralised by Q4 if prices return toward original forecast. Management said it could not fully absorb the fuel increase.
Management said Q3 and Q4 are the strong quarters (wedding season, Diwali, Christmas, New Year), but declined to give forward booking numbers.
Management said it expects cruise operating margins of about 35% or higher, versus a global range of 35% to 40%.
Fuel cost impact of about Rs 12 crore is expected to remain in the current period after surcharges, per the CFO's answer on Q1 and Q2 impact.
SUN delivery remains on schedule for about 11 months from the call.
capex_capacity: Cordelia Sky (2,400 guests, 1,002 staterooms) delivered early and arrived in Mumbai on the call date; sailing starts 23 October 2026. Capacity rises about 126%.
SUN, a sister ship of Sky, is due in about 11 months, on schedule.
Advance of Rs 4,290 million toward acquisition of new vessels, interest-bearing, held through a subsidiary and an intermediary; not yet used as of the call.

Management is exploring fleet expansion beyond SUN and is at an initial discussion stage. Financing options: lease structure (fixed lease over 10 years, dollar buyout at year 10), internal accruals, or outright purchase with debt.
Sky lease cost is about USD 16 million per year, treated as an operating cost in management's numbers under Ind AS.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per passenger rose to Rs 13,645 in Q2 FY27 from Rs 10,349, driven by higher ticket price and onboard revenue.
Company started charging a fuel surcharge of USD 15-20 per person per day to offset part of the fuel cost increase.
Sky's per-guest pricing is said to be about 100% higher than Empress, and SUN's about 150% higher, driven by cabin mix (suites: 60/69 on Empress, 260 on Sky, 600 on SUN).

Management said the Indian overnight ocean and coastal cruise market was about Rs 8,301 million in FY25 and is expected to grow 20-25% CAGR over FY26-FY31. India had about 4.8 lakh cruise passenger movements in CY2025, about 89% domestic.
Management cited about 95 wedding dates in FY28 versus a typical 65-70, and plans to grow weddings and celebrations as a revenue stream.
Loyalty programme 'Chairman's Club' is being rolled out.

qa_highlights.question: How much margin expansion from operating leverage, and how will fuel, crew and port costs be controlled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cruise margins globally are 35-40% and the company expects to match or beat that. Shared corporate costs across more ships are expected to lower per-ship operating cost. Fuel is expected to ease, and the company plans to offset it with surcharges, itinerary changes and cost savings.

qa_highlights.question: How will the next fleet addition be financed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the lease structure used for Empress, Sky and SUN (fixed lease over 10 years, then a nominal buyout). It also cited internal accruals (about Rs 220 crore used for Sky and SUN pre-IPO) and possible debt funding for an outright purchase.

qa_highlights.question: Why did short-term borrowings rise by about Rs 344 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the funds were advanced to a subsidiary, which passed them to an intermediary to hold ready for an identified vessel deal. The money is interest-bearing and not yet used.

qa_highlights.question: How much fuel cost is unrecovered and what price increase would neutralise it?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said about Rs 12 crore of fuel cost impact remains after surcharges and savings. Management said full absorption is unlikely and it hopes to return to original forecast by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How does lease cost for Sky and SUN affect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Sky lease is about USD 16 million per year. Management said it is included in operating costs and pricing, and below EBITDA under Ind AS it is absorbed at PBT and PAT levels.

qa_highlights.question: What are the bookings for H2, including Empress and Sky?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give forward numbers, citing restrictions on forward-looking statements. It said demand was strong and that near-term bookings were hard to get.

risks_watch: Fuel cost unrecovered: management said about Rs 12 crore of fuel impact stays in the current period after surcharges, versus about Rs 28 crore for H1, and full absorption is not expected; watch whether Q3 and Q4 fuel costs ease toward the original forecast.

Rs 4,290 million advance for new vessel acquisition is interest-bearing, not yet used, and the counterparty and asset are undisclosed; watch deal completion, financing structure (lease vs outright purchase vs internal accruals) and the short-term borrowing build-up.

Sky ramp-up: revenue contribution starts H2 FY27 with a Sky lease cost of about USD 16 million per year; watch Sky utilisation, pricing, and the fuel-surcharge (USD 15-20 per person per day) effect on demand.
SUN delivery due in about 11 months, and further fleet expansion is at an early discussion stage; watch timing and funding for both.
Management declined to give forward bookings for H2; watch Q3 and Q4 (wedding season, Diwali, Christmas, New Year) realisation against the 35% or higher cruise margin target.
key_quotes: Very pleased to say a key development as we enter the second half of FY27 is the delivery of Cordelia Sky, which has arrived in Mumbai today this morning at 8:00 A.M.

We are very hopeful that Q3 and Q4 outlook for fuel will be reduced a little bit and our profit margin will increase due to that. However, we are not 100% certain if the geopolitical situation is changing that fast.
Well, as you know, we're not allowed to make any forward statements.
So, this impact of 12 odd crores will remain.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the Sky delivery, Q2 growth and the long-term cruise opportunity, but cautious and evasive on forward bookings, fuel price direction and the identity of the vessel and financing counterparties. Answers on fuel recovery were hedged with hopes rather than figures.
